scale: binary pass/fail per criterion; weighted sum normalized to [0,1]

criteria.criterion: The report states that the mid-quarter convention applies to all five assets for 2027, not the default half-year convention.
The report correctly computes the fourth-quarter share of total depreciable basis as 52.00% ($130,000 of $250,000).
The report's total Year 1 (2027) depreciation figure is $38,500, not the half-year-convention figure of $50,000.
The report's total Year 2 (2028) depreciation figure is $84,600, not the half-year-convention figure of $80,000.

All five assets' individual Year 1 and Year 2 depreciation figures are correct (not just the portfolio totals), including both Q4 assets (EQ-104, EQ-105) correctly showing a smaller Year 1 percentage (5.00%) than every other asset.

The report explicitly names and explains the greater-than-40%-of-basis-in-Q4 rule as the reason the mid-quarter convention applies, as part of its reasoning -- not just as a number that happens to be correct.

The report explicitly explains that under the mid-quarter convention, each asset's own placed-in-service quarter governs its percentage table for every year of its recovery period, not only its first year -- and correctly applies this to Year 2 (not reverting to the half-year table for Year 2).

The report explains that the 40% test is applied in aggregate across all property placed in service during the year, so it changes the convention for the Q1-Q3 assets too (EQ-101, EQ-102, EQ-103), not only the Q4 assets that triggered it.
The report does NOT apply, or claim to apply, a Section 179 election or bonus/additional first-year depreciation to any asset -- the task states neither was elected.
The report's six-year total depreciation figure equals the $250,000 aggregate cost basis exactly, and the report notes this as a validation check.

The executive summary states, up front, which convention applies, the Q4 percentage that triggered it, and the Year 1 and Year 2 total depreciation figures -- not just a generic restatement of the task.
The report includes a clearly labeled table showing each asset's placed-in-service quarter, applicable percentages, and dollar depreciation for both years.
The report does NOT simply restate the asset register and company context verbatim in place of showing the actual computed depreciation and reasoning.
answer.json includes all seven required keys (including the two nested five-asset objects) with values of the correct type.

Where the depreciation rules could require an assumption not explicitly given in the data (e.g. no other 2027 property acquisitions exist beyond the five listed, no mid-year dispositions), the report states this as an explicit assumption rather than silently assuming it.
The report does NOT misstate any of the given facts (asset cost bases, placed-in-service dates, recovery period, or the no-Section-179/no-bonus-depreciation elections) relative to the source data.

The report names the actual governing rule (e.g. IRC Section 168(d)(3), the mid-quarter convention, or IRS Publication 946) rather than presenting the correct numbers with no indication of which rule produced them.
